newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate slides 40 bps to 10.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate slides 40 bps to 10.0 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slid 40 basis points to 10.0 percent on Thursday due to weaker demand for longer-term kuna.
Dealers put the daily settlements at 47.2 million kuna, half of which was call money at an unchanged 8.0 percent rate. Fresh transactions accounted for all but 9.5 million.
Supply totalled 52 million kuna, against demand for 53 million, but one foreign bank refused to lend money to some savings banks, which had overshot their debt limits.
The one-day interbank rate was stable at 8.0 percent and six-ten day rates ranged between 10 and 11 percent depending on the borrower.
One-month money was rolled over at 14.5-17 percent.
Insurers' renewed 30-day deals at a slightly lower 12-percent rate, compared to 13 on Wednesday.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates firmer at 6.2777 against the dollar and a touch weaker at 3.5681 against the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
